tools.name: search_servers
tools.description: Use when the user needs an MCP server for a task, or asks whether one exists, works today, or needs a key or sign-in. Do not use for general web search; for one server already known by name use get_server. Find remote MCP servers listed in the Official MCP Registry, with MCP Station's daily measurem

tools.name: search_tools
tools.description: Use when the user needs a specific capability (a tool) rather than a whole server; to find servers by topic use search_servers. Find individual tools by name and description (as the servers report them in tools/list), with the server each belongs to and its measurements. Example: q='pdf table extrac

tools.name: get_server
tools.description: Use before connecting a server, or when the user names one: registry data, latest measurements, declared risk, rank parts, connection URLs and tools of one server.

tools.name: get_server_history
tools.description: Use when the user asks whether a server has been answering lately: daily check results (reachable, response time) of one server for up to 30 days.

tools.name: get_changes
tools.description: Use when the user asks what changed in the servers they use, or wants to review tool changes before using a server again. Tools added or removed, input schema changes, new destructive tools, servers that stopped or started answering, and new listings, per day for the last 30 days. Give names to watc

tools.name: check_overlap
tools.description: Use when the user has several MCP servers connected or planned and wants to know if any duplicate each other. Give the exact registry names of the MCP servers you connect (or plan to). Returns which of them share tool definitions, a remote endpoint or a registry description, compared on the same mea

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: Use to browse what kinds of MCP servers exist or to get category IDs for search filters: category IDs (stable), names, parents and server counts.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_changes" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Use when the user asks what changed in the servers they use, or wants to review tool changes before using a server again. Tools added or removed, input schema c…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_server, get_changes · Private data: search_servers · Public sink: check_overlap.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_server, get_changes · Private data: search_servers · Public sink: check_overlap

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_servers" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
